overview: Cote d'Ivoire's women's health landscape is anchored by a strong public-policy push, free family planning in the public sector since a 2024 decree, national campaigns to cut unintended pregnancies, and one of Africa's largest HPV vaccination drives, rather than by a dense pool of homegrown femtech startups. The most globally significant asset is Abidjan-based Janngo Capital, Africa's largest gender-equal tech VC fund, which channels capital into women-benefiting health and digital services across francophone Africa. Digital and maternal-health innovation is emerging through platforms like La Case Maternelle and pan-African entrants such as GiftedMom/Healthlane, alongside a growing e-sante and telemedicine ecosystem. Menstrual health is served mainly by NGOs and civil-society associations concentrated in Abidjan.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent headlines center on reproductive-health campaigns, cervical-cancer prevention, and the buildout of digital health infrastructure.

items.text: Gavi and the government launched Cote d'Ivoire's largest HPV vaccination campaign to date (April 7 to 13), targeting 3.5 million girls aged 10 to 18, in and out of school.

National Family Planning Campaign (SNPF, Nov 27 to Dec 2) launched from Abobo to accelerate free access to sexual and reproductive health services across ten health regions including Abidjan, Daloa, Yamoussoukro and San-Pedro.
UAmC-CI project (Universal Access to Modern Contraception) officially launched at Dabou General Hospital, running July 2025 to March 2028 to consolidate free family planning.
A telemedicine digital-health platform announced its official go-live for June 8, 2026, aiming to connect health professionals with populations in remote areas.
WHO reported Cote d'Ivoire extending cervical-cancer screening via HPV self-testing, letting women collect their own samples.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: National strategy pairs universal health coverage with free reproductive services and a digital-health agenda.

items.text: Decree signed establishing free family planning services in the public sector, the basis for subsequent scale-up projects.
PNDS 2021-2025 (National Health Development Plan) embeds digital health within its governance axis, covering a National e-health project, telemedicine, and an electronic vaccination record.
Reproductive-health target: raise modern contraceptive prevalence from 25.5% (2022) to 32.3% by end of 2025 amid 2.9% annual demographic growth.
Budgeted National Family Planning Action Plan (PANB 2021-2025) published by the Ministry of Health, setting national FP commitments.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Digital-health infrastructure and startup support programs are expanding, though dedicated femtech ventures remain few.

items.text: Direction de l'Informatique et de la Sante Digitale (DISD) established within the Ministry of Health to steer telemedicine and digital-health deployment nationwide.
Orange Fab Cote d'Ivoire, the Orange Group's first startup accelerator in Africa, has backed 20-plus startups including e-health ventures and partners with Seedstars.
GiftedMom pivoted to Healthlane in 2024, an AI healthtech platform (menstrual tracking, multilingual health Q&A, e-pharmacy) operating across Cote d'Ivoire, Nigeria and Cameroon.
TechMousso gender-data competition in Abidjan (Data2X, World Wide Web Foundation, MCC) paired local developers with civil-society groups on women's issues, awarding a $10,000 top prize.
La Case Maternelle grew into a leading maternal-health education platform with over 177,000 Facebook followers.
